panic.ety:
The adjective is borrowed from Middle French panique, a word itself borrowed from Ancient Greek πανικός (panikós, “pertaining to Pan”); Pan, the Greek god of fields and woods, was believed to be the source of mysterious sounds that caused contagious, groundless fear in herds and crowds, or in people in lonely spots.
Adjective sense 3 (“pertaining to or resulting from overpowering fear or fright”) is partly an attributive use of the noun.
The noun is derived from the adjective, while the verb is derived from the noun. Verb sense 1.3 (“to highly amuse, entertain, or impress (an audience watching

ex.en: He had words with his employer and was fired.
ex.ja: 彼は雇い主と口論して首になった。

ex.en: The employer made a new offer to the workers.
ex.ja: 雇い主は労働者に新しい提案をした。

note.ja: em（中に）+ ploy（折る）+ er。仕事に巻き込む側の人 →「雇い主」。employee（雇われる人）と対。

en: Extremely large; greatly exceeding the common size, extent, etc.

enormous.ety: From Latin ēnormis. An assimilated form of ex- (“out of”) + norma (“rule, norm”) + -ous.

ex.en: The damage of the disaster has been enormous.
ex.ja: その災害の被害はべらぼうに大きかった。

ex.en: He lives in an enormous house.
ex.ja: 彼は巨大な家に住んでいる。

ex.en: Tom lives in an enormous house.
ex.ja: トムは巨大な家に住んでいる。

note.ja: e（外へ）+ norm（基準）+ ous。基準から外れた →「巨大な・莫大な」。normal（基準どおりの→普通の）も同じ norm。

en: To pardon (someone); to waive any negative feeling towards or desire for punishment or retribution against.
To pardon (something); to waive any negative feeling over or retribution for.

forgive.ety: Alteration (due to give) of Middle English foryiven, forȝiven, from Old English forġiefan (“to forgive, to give”), from Proto-West Germanic *frageban, from Proto-Germanic *fragebaną (“to give away; give up; release; forgive”), equivalent to for- + give (etymologically for- + yive). Cognate with Scots forgeve, forgif, forgie (“to forgive”), West Frisian ferjaan (“to forgive”), Dutch vergeven (“to forgive”), German vergeben (“to forgive”), Icelandic fyrirgefa (“to forgive”), Yiddish פֿאַרגעבן (fargebn, “to forgive”)

ex.en: In any case, I've already entirely forgiven you.
ex.ja: とにかく、君のことは、もうすべて許したんだ。

ex.en: I can't forgive him for what he did.
ex.ja: 私は彼のしたことを許せない。

ex.en: He isn't going to forgive me so easily.
ex.ja: 彼はそう簡単に私を許してはくれないでしょう。

A petrol filling station.
To store in a garage.

ex.en: The car is in front of the garage.
ex.ja: 車はガレージの前だよ。

ex.en: Can you imagine Tom working in a garage?
ex.ja: トムが自動車修理工場で働いているなんて想像できますか。

en: A non-specific rule or principle that provides direction to action or behaviour.
A plan or explanation to guide one in setting standards or determining a course of action.
To provide guidelines for.
The act of inquiring; a seeking of information by asking questions; interrogation; a question or questioning.
A search for truth, information, or knowledge; examination of facts or principles; research; investigation; inquest.

inquiry.ety: From Middle English enquery, from the Old French verb enquerre, from Latin inquīrō, composed of in- (“in, at, on; into”) + quaerō (“to seek, look for”), of uncertain origin, but possibly from Proto-Italic *kʷaizeō, from Proto-Indo-European *kʷeh₂- (“to acquire”). Later respelled to conform to the original Latin spelling, as opposed to the Old French spelling.

ex.en: He wrote a letter of inquiry to his business contact.
ex.ja: 彼は取引先に照会状を書いた。

ex.en: We made inquiries into his past.
ex.ja: 彼の前歴について私たちは調査した。

ex.en: Thank you for your inquiry.
ex.ja: お問い合わせいただきありがとうございます。

note.ja: in（中へ）+ quir（求める）+ y。中を求めて尋ねること →「問い合わせ・調査」。

en: A person employed to inspect something.
A police officer ranking below superintendent.

inspector.ety: Borrowed from Latin īnspector, from īnspiciō, equivalent to inspect + -or.

ex.en: The suspect told a lie to the inspector.
ex.ja: 容疑者は捜査官にうそを言った。

ex.en: The inspector arrived at the school late on Monday morning.
ex.ja: 調査官は月曜の午前の遅い時間にその学校に到着した。

ex.en: He is a sanitary inspector.
ex.ja: 彼は衛生監視員である。

en: A big cat, Panthera leo, native to Africa, India and formerly much of Europe.
A male lion, as opposed to a lioness, which is characterized by having a flowing shaggy mane and taking little part in hunting, which can…
Of the light brown color that resembles the fur of a lion.

lion.ety: From Middle English lyoun, lion, leon, borrowed from Old French lion, from Latin leō, (accusative: leōnem), from Ancient Greek λέων (léōn), of unclear origin. Doublet of Leo, leu, lev, and Lyon. Displaced Old English lēo, from the same Latin source.

ex.en: The lion is called the king of animals.
ex.ja: ライオンは百獣の王と呼ばれている。

ex.en: I was surprised to see a lion.
ex.ja: 私はライオンを見て驚いた。

ex.en: Joe and I saw a lion yesterday.
ex.ja: ジョーと僕は昨日ライオンを見ました。

en: Unhappy due to feeling isolated from contact with other people.
Unfrequented by people; desolate.

lonely.ety: From lone + -ly, or from an apheretic shortening of alonely. See lone.

ex.en: I was lonely, with nobody to play with.
ex.ja: 遊び相手がなくて孤独だった。

ex.en: Since Tom has left, I've been very lonely.
ex.ja: トムが去ってからというもの、とても寂しくてね。

ex.en: He lives in this lonely place by himself.
ex.ja: 彼は一人でこの寂しい場所に住んでいます。

en: Relenting; forbearance to cause or allow harm to another.
Forgiveness or compassion, especially toward those less fortunate.
To feel mercy
To show mercy; to pardon or treat leniently because of mercy
Expressing surprise or alarm.

mercy.ety: From Middle English mercy, merci, from Anglo-Norman merci (compare continental Old French merci, mercit), from Latin mercēs (“wages, fee, price”), from merx (“wares, merchandise”). Displaced native Old English mildheortnes (literally "mildheartedness"). Cognate with French merci, whence the doublet merci.

ex.en: Man is indeed at the mercy of nature.
ex.ja: 人間は実際自然のなすがままである。

ex.en: Farmers are always at the mercy of the weather.
ex.ja: 農民たちはいつも天候のなすがままになる。

ex.en: Beer sales are at the mercy of the weather.
ex.ja: ビールの売れ行きは天候しだいです。

en: In spite of what preceded; yet.

nevertheless.ety: From Middle English nevertheles, never-þe-les, nevere-þe-lesse. By surface analysis, never (“not at all”) + the + less; compare never the wiser.

ex.en: Nevertheless, I want to go there.
ex.ja: それでも、そこに行ってみたい。

ex.en: I was very tired, but I was nevertheless unable to sleep.
ex.ja: 私は疲れていたが、それにもかかわらず眠れなかった。

ex.en: We thought it would rain; nevertheless, we started on our trip.
ex.ja: 雨が降るだろうと思っていたのだが、それでも旅行に出かけた。

en: The chemical element (symbol O) with an atomic number of 8 and relative atomic mass of 15.9994. It is a colorless and odorless gas. Somet…
Molecular oxygen (O₂), a colorless, odorless gas at room temperature.

oxygen.ety:

Ancient Greek ὀξύς (oxús)

Borrowed from French oxygène (originally in the form principe oxygène, a variant of principe oxigine ‘acidifying principle’, suggested by Lavoisier), from Ancient Greek ὀξύς (oxús, “sharp”) + γένος (génos, “birth”), referring to oxygen's supposed role in the formation of acids. By surface analysis, oxy- + -gen.

ex.en: Plants give off oxygen as they make food.
ex.ja: 植物は栄養物を作っているとき、酸素を放出する。

ex.en: No living things could live without oxygen.
ex.ja: 生物は酸素なしでは生きられない。

ex.en: You cannot burn anything without oxygen.
ex.ja: 酸素がないと何も燃やせない。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 oxys（鋭い・酸っぱい）+ gen（生む）。「酸を生むもの」と考えられて名付けられた →「酸素」。hydrogen（水を生むもの→水素）も同じ gen。

en: A wind instrument consisting of a tube, often lined with holes to allow for adjustment in pitch, sounded by blowing into the tube.
A tube used to produce sound in an organ; an organ pipe.
To play (music) on a pipe instrument, such as a bagpipe or a flute.
To shout loudly and at high pitch.

pipe.ety:
From Middle English pīpe, pype (“hollow cylinder or tube used as a conduit or container; duct or vessel of the body; musical instrument; financial records maintained by the English Exchequer, pipe roll”), from Old English pīpe (“pipe (musical instrument); the channel of a small stream”), from Proto-West Germanic *pīpā. Reinforced by Vulgar Latin *pīpa, from Latin pipire, pipiare, pipare, from pīpiō (“to chirp, peep”), of imitative origin. Displaced native Old English fealh and Old English þrūh. Doublet of fife.
Cognate with Dutch pijp, German Pfeife, Danish pibe, Norwegian Bokmål and Norwegian

ex.en: He spoke with a pipe in his mouth.
ex.ja: 彼はパイプをくわえて話した。

ex.en: The oil ran through a thick pipe.
ex.ja: 石油が太いパイプの中を流れた。

ex.en: The pipe shop is across the street.
ex.ja: パイプ屋は通りの向こう側です。

piss.ety: From Middle English pisse (noun) and pissen (verb), from Old French pissier, possibly from Vulgar Latin *pīssiāre, probably of imitative origin. Compare Old Norse pissa (“to urinate, piss”). Displaced Old English miċġe (“urine”) and mīgan (“to urinate”).

ex.en: People like you piss me off the most.
ex.ja: お前みたいな奴が一番むかつくんだよ。

ex.en: Do you sometimes get pissed off for no reason?
ex.ja: たまに訳もなくイライラすることってない？

ex.en: Can I go to the bathroom? I gotta piss.
ex.ja: トイレに行ってもいい？おしっこしたい。

en: A literary piece written in verse.
A piece of writing in the tradition of poetry, an instance of poetry.

poem.ety: From Middle French poème, from Latin poēma, from Ancient Greek ποίημα (poíēma), from ποιέω (poiéō, “to make”). Widely displaced English leed.

ex.en: She taught me how to write a poem.
ex.ja: 彼女は私に詩の書き方を教えてくれた。

ex.en: He read the poem with a loud voice.
ex.ja: 彼は高らかにその詩を読み上げた。

ex.en: He taught me how to write a poem.
ex.ja: 彼は私に詩の書き方を教えてくれた。

en: The fine particles which are the result of reducing a dry substance by pounding, grinding, or triturating, or the result of decay; dust.
A mixture of fine dry, sweet-smelling particles applied to the face or other body parts, to reduce shine or to alleviate chaffing.
To reduce to fine particles; to pound, grind, or rub into a powder.
To sprinkle with powder, or as if with powder.

powder.ety: From Middle English poudre, pouder, pouldre, borrowed from Old French poudre, poldre, puldre, from Latin pulverem, accusative singular of Latin pulvis (“dust, powder”). Doublet of pulver. Compare pollen (“fine flour”), polverine, pulverize.

ex.en: You have to take this powder after each meal.
ex.ja: この粉薬は毎食後飲んでください。

ex.en: I have trouble taking powdered medicine.
ex.ja: 私、粉薬って苦手なのよね。

ex.en: Shall I go to the powder room for a moment, I wonder.
ex.ja: ちょっと、トイレ行ってこようっと。

en: The belief that there are distinct human races with inherent differences which determine their abilities, and generally that some are sup…
The policies, practices, or systems (e.g. government or political) promoting this belief or promoting the dominance of one or more races …

racism.ety: Borrowed from French racisme, equivalent to race + -ism.

en: Lacking in refinement or civility; bad-mannered; discourteous.
Lacking refinement or skill; untaught; ignorant; raw.

rude.ety: From Middle English rude, from Old French rude, ruide, from Latin rudis (“rough, raw, rude, wild, untilled”).

ex.en: You shouldn't say such rude things to him.
ex.ja: 彼にそんな失礼なことを言うものではない。

ex.en: I think it would be rude to refuse.
ex.ja: 断るのは失礼なんじゃないかな。

ex.en: Nothing can excuse him for such rude behavior.
ex.ja: この様な彼の無礼な行為はどんなことがあっても許されない。

en: A simple machine, a helical inclined plane.
A (usually) metal fastener consisting of a partially or completely threaded shank, sometimes with a threaded point, and a head used to bo…
To connect or assemble pieces using a screw.
To extort or practice extortion upon; to oppress by unreasonable or extortionate exactions; to put the screws on.

ex.en: He seems like he's got a few screws loose.
ex.ja: 彼は風変わりな奴だ。

ex.en: When I turned the screw, water burst out.
ex.ja: 僕がネジを回すと水が吹き出してきた。

ex.en: I screwed up my courage and went there.
ex.ja: 私は思い切ってそこに行った。

en: The ordinal form of the number seven.
The person or thing in the seventh position.
One of seven equal parts of a whole.

seventh.ety: From Middle English seventhe, sefte, from Old English seofoþa, from Proto-West Germanic *sebundō, from Proto-Germanic *sebundô. The -n-, lost in northern Proto-West Germanic, was later reinserted by analogy with seven, equivalent to seven + -th.

ex.en: We arrived on the morning of the seventh.
ex.ja: 私たちは７日の朝到着した。

ex.en: July is the seventh month of the year.
ex.ja: 「７月」は１年の中で７回目の月にあたります。

ex.en: The seventh day of the week is Saturday.
ex.ja: 週の７番目の日は土曜日です。

en: A place where a person or animal may find protection from the elements (especially rain, storms, or cold) sometimes as a place to sleep (…
A bare-bones above-ground structure meant to provide temporary cover from the elements; usually small and with no door to close.
To provide cover from damage or harassment; to shield; to protect.
To take cover.

shelter.ety:
From Middle English sheltron, sheldtrume (“roof or wall formed by locked shields”), from Old English sċildtruma, sċyldtruma (“a phalanx, company (of troops), a tortoise, a covering, shed, shelter”, literally “shield-troop”), from sċyld, sċield (“shield”) + truma (“a troop of soldiers”). Cognate with Scots schilthrum, schiltrum. More at shield, and Old English trymman (“to strengthen”), from trum (“strong, firm”) at trim.
Doublet of sheltron (a kind of military formation), which is the more conservative of the two.

ex.en: I had to take shelter under a tree.
ex.ja: 木の下で雨宿りしなければなりませんでした。

ex.en: These flowers should be sheltered from the rain.
ex.ja: その花は雨に当ててはいけない。

ex.en: Shelters have been built in fear of war.
ex.ja: 戦争を恐れてシェルターが作られてきた。

en: A person's name, written by that person, used as identification or to signify approval of accompanying material, such as a legal contract.
An act of signing one's name; an act of producing a signature.
Distinctive, characteristic, indicative of identity.
To sign with one's signature, to write one's signature on.

signature.ety: Borrowed from Middle French signature, or from Medieval Latin signātūra, future active periphrastic of verb signāre from signum (“sign”), + -tūra, feminine of -tūrus, future active periphrastic suffix. Displaced native Old English handseten (literally “hand setting”).

ex.en: Please return one set to us with your signature.
ex.ja: 一通に署名の上ご返送ください。

ex.en: I attached my signature to the document.
ex.ja: 私は書類に署名した。

ex.en: May I have your signature here, please?
ex.ja: こちらにサインを頂けますでしょうか。

note.ja: sign（印）+ at + ure。自分の印をつけること →「署名」。

en: Any of various eight-legged, predatory arthropods, of the order Araneae, most of which spin webs to catch prey.
A float (drink) made by mixing ice-cream and a soda or fizzy drink (such as lemonade).
To move like a spider.
To cover a surface like a cobweb.

spider.ety:
Inherited from Middle English spithre, spider, from Old English spīþra (“spider”), from Proto-West Germanic *spinþrijō, from Proto-Germanic *spinnaną (“to spin”). Mostly displaced attercop (“spider, unpleasant person”), now a dialectal term.
Compare typologically Proto-Slavic *mězgyrь (whence Russian мизги́рь (mizgírʹ)) (akin to Latvian mežģīt), Turkish örümcek (akin to örmek).

ex.en: There are people that are afraid of spiders.
ex.ja: クモが怖い人もいる。

ex.en: One of my favorite songs is Hungry Spider.
ex.ja: 私の好きな曲はハングリー・スパイダーです。

ex.en: I just saw a really scary spider.
ex.ja: マジでおっかない蜘蛛がいた。

en: An acknowledgment of gratitude, respect or admiration; an accompanying gift.
An homage made in a body of work to another work or creator.
To pay (something) as tribute.

tribute.ety: From Middle English tribut (14th c.), from Middle French tribut, from Latin tributum (“tribute”, literally “a thing contributed or paid”), past participle of tribuere (“to assign, allot”), usually derived from tribus (whence English tribe).

ex.en: The verdict is a tribute to their fairness.
ex.ja: 評決は公平な審議の証拠である。

note.ja: ラテン語 tribuere（割り当てる・与える）から。割り当てて納めるもの →「貢ぎ物」→ 敬意として捧げるもの →「賛辞・敬意」。

en: A finger-operated lever used to fire a gun.
A similar device used to activate any mechanism.
To fire (a weapon); to set off or trip (a mechanism or function of a device).
To cause, to precipitate, to bring (something) about in response or as a result.

trigger.ety: Originally tricker, from Dutch trekker (“pull”, noun, as in drawer-pull, bell-pull), from Dutch trekken (“to drag, draw, pull”).

ex.en: I pulled the trigger again and again.
ex.ja: 私は連続で引き金を引いた。

ex.en: We will trigger a revolution in the IT industry.
ex.ja: ITのマーケットプレイスに革命を起こす。

ex.en: Police can't be trigger happy.
ex.ja: 警察は簡単に銃を使ってはいけない。

en: To change with time or a similar parameter.
To institute a change in, from a current state; to modify.

vary.ety: From Middle English varien, from Old French varier, from Latin variō (“to change, alter, make different”), from varius (“different, various”); see various.

ex.en: It includes widely varying organizations, people, and ideas.
ex.ja: これには、様々な種類の団体、人々、考え方が含まれている。

ex.en: These shoes vary in size, but not in shape.
ex.ja: これらの靴は大きさは違うが形は違わない。

ex.en: Your philosophy of life varies from mine.
ex.ja: 君の人生観は僕のと違っているね。

en: A theater, auditorium, arena, or other area designated for sporting or entertainment events.
A neighborhood or near place; the place or county in which anything is alleged to have happened; also, the place where an action is laid,…

venue.ety: From Middle English venu, from Old French venue, the feminine singular past participle of the verb venir (to come). Doublet of veny.

ex.en: The inside of the venue was silent.
ex.ja: 会場内は、シーンと静まり返っていました。

ex.en: At the venue, the scene was quiet.
ex.ja: 会場内は、シーンと静まり返っていました。

ex.en: In the venue, it was pure silence.
ex.ja: 会場内は、シーンと静まり返っていました。

en: A spontaneous abortion; a miscarriage.
An induced abortion.

abortion.ety: From Latin abortiōnem (“miscarriage, abortion”), from aborior (“to miscarry”). Equivalent to abort + -ion. Displaced native Old English ǣwyrp (literally “throwing out, rejection”).

ex.en: People are taking sides on the abortion issue.
ex.ja: 中絶問題で議論が二分しています。

ex.en: I had an abortion two years ago.
ex.ja: ２年前中絶しました。

ex.en: Are you for or against abortions?
ex.ja: あなたは妊娠中絶に賛成ですか、反対ですか。

en: The state of being accurate; being free from error; exactness; correctness
Exact conformity to truth, or to a rule or model; degree of conformity of a measure to a true or standard value.

ex.en: Check up on the accuracy of this article.
ex.ja: この記事が何処まで本当か調べてくれ。

ex.en: I began to doubt the accuracy of his statement.
ex.ja: 私は彼の陳述の正確さを疑い始めた。

ex.en: He reported the details with accuracy.
ex.ja: 彼はその詳細を正確に報告した。

Insincere; fake, forced, or feigned.

ex.en: I found them lying on the artificial grass.
ex.ja: 彼らは人工芝の上に横たわっていた。

en: Below or underneath.
Below.
In a position that is lower in rank, dignity, etc.

beneath.ety: From Middle English benethe, from Old English bineoþan (“beneath, under, below”), equivalent to be- + neath. Cognate with Low German benedden (“beneath”), Dutch beneden (“beneath, under, down”), obsolete German benieden (“below”).

ex.en: It is beneath you to say such a thing.
ex.ja: そういうことを言うのは君らしくない。

ex.en: The ice will crack beneath our weight.
ex.ja: 我々の重みで氷が割れるだろう。

ex.en: He took it from beneath his coat.
ex.ja: 彼はそれを上着の下から出した。

To provide with, usually for a specific purpose.

outfit.ety: Variant of earlier out-fit, from fit out. Equivalent to out- + fit.

ex.en: What do you think of this outfit?
ex.ja: この衣装どう思う？

ex.en: That outfit is running a fly-by-night operation.
ex.ja: あの会社は先行き不安な商売をしています。

ex.en: Do you have an outfit to wear to the dance?
ex.ja: ダンスに着ていく服はあるの？

en: An annuity paid regularly as benefit due to a retired employee, serviceman etc. in consideration of past services, originally and chiefly…
A sum paid to a clergyman in place of tithes.
To grant a pension to.
To force (someone) to retire on a pension.

pension.ety: From Middle English pencioun, pensioun, from Anglo-Norman pencione, Old French pencion, and their source, Latin pēnsiō (“payment, weight, rent, compensation”), from the participle stem of pendō (“to weigh”). Doublet of pensione.

ex.en: People 65 and above get a pension from the government.
ex.ja: ６５歳以上の人たちは政府から年金を受けている。

ex.en: The old man lives on his pension.
ex.ja: その老人は年金で暮らしている。

ex.en: She has to live on the pension.
ex.ja: 彼女は年金で生計を立てなければならない。

note.ja: pens（支払う）+ ion。定期的に支払われるもの →「年金」。フランス語では「下宿（料金を払う宿）」の意も。

en: To allow (something) to happen, to give permission for.
To allow (someone) to do something; to give permission to.
An artifact or document rendering something allowed or legal.
A learner's permit.

permit.ety: From Middle English permitten, borrowed from Middle French permettre, from Latin permittō (“give up, allow”), from per (“through”) + mittō (“send”).

ex.en: The teacher didn't permit me to leave early.
ex.ja: 先生は私が早く帰るのを許可しなかった。

ex.en: Do you have a permit for a gun?
ex.ja: 銃の許可書はお持ちですか？

ex.en: Please permit me to ask you some questions.
ex.ja: いくつか質問させてください。

note.ja: per（通して）+ mit（送る）。通して行かせる →「許可する・許可証」。

en: Giving pleasure; pleasing in manner.

pleasant.ety: From Middle English plesaunte, from Old French plaisant. By surface analysis, please + -ant. Related to Dutch plezant (“full of fun or pleasure”). Partly displaced Old English wynsum, which became Modern English winsome.

ex.en: I found it pleasant walking in the country.
ex.ja: 田園を歩くのは楽しいと思った。

ex.en: These records will make for a pleasant party.
ex.ja: これらのレコードはパーティーを楽しくするのに役立つだろう。

ex.en: It is pleasant to sleep under the tree.
ex.ja: その木の木陰で寝るのは気持ちいい。

en: A painting or other picture of a person, especially the head and shoulders.
An accurate depiction of a person, a mood, etc.
Representing the actual features of an individual; not ideal.

portrait.ety:
From Middle French portraict, pourtraict, nominal use of the past participle of portraire (“portray”), from Latin prōtrahō (< prō- + trahō).
Compare typologically English drawing.

ex.en: This portrait is nearly as large as life.
ex.ja: この肖像画はほぼ実物大です。

ex.en: The portrait of her was true to life.
ex.ja: 彼女の肖像画は本物そっくりだった。

ex.en: This is a portrait of my late father.
ex.ja: これは亡くなった父の肖像画です。

note.ja: por（= pro 前へ）+ trait（引く・描く）。前へ引き出して描いたもの →「肖像画・描写」。

en: Capable of producing something, especially in abundance; fertile.
Yielding good or useful results; constructive.

ex.ja: 現場は開発に積極的だった。

ex.ja: アメリカ人は人生のほとんどを働き、生産しながら過ごす。

ex.en: The site was productive in development.
ex.ja: 現場は開発に積極的だった。

note.ja: pro（前へ）+ duct（導く）+ ive。たくさん生み出す →「生産的な・実りある」。

en: In a safe manner; without risk; using caution above all else.
In a secure manner; without the possibility of injury or harm resulting.

safely.ety: From Middle English savely; equivalent to safe + -ly.

ex.en: He returned home safely, which pleased his parents.
ex.ja: 彼は無事帰ってきた。それで両親は喜んだ。

ex.en: I'm sure of his returning home safely.
ex.ja: 彼はきっと無事に帰って来るよ。

ex.en: Make certain that he returned home safely.
ex.ja: 彼が無事に帰宅したか確かめなさい。

en: Minor; small in amount
Gentle or weak, not aggressive or powerful.
To treat as unimportant or not worthy of attention; to make light of.
To give lesser weight or importance to.
The act of ignoring or snubbing; a deliberate act of neglect or discourtesy.

slight.ety: From Middle English slight (“bad, of poor quality, unimportant, trivial, slender, slim, smooth, level”), from Old English sliht (“smooth, level”), from Proto-Germanic *slihtaz (“slippery, flat, level, plain”), related to English slick. Cognate with Scots slicht (“bad, of poor quality”), West Frisian sljocht (“smooth, level, plain, simple”), Dutch slecht (“bad”), Low German slecht (“bad”), German schlecht (“bad”) and schlicht (“plain, artless, natural”), Danish slet (“bad, evil, poor, nasty, wrong”), Swedish slät (“smooth”), Norwegian Bokmål and Norwegian Nynorsk slett (“even”), Icelandic slétt

ex.en: I'm not worried about that in the slightest.
ex.ja: それについては、これっぽっちも心配してない。

ex.en: I have a slight pain in my side.
ex.ja: 脇腹が少し痛い。

ex.en: My tennis hasn't improved in the slightest.
ex.ja: 私のテニスは少しも上達していない。

ex.ja: ＵＳＳＲはソビエト社会主義共和国連邦を表しています。

en: To file a legal action against someone, generally a non-criminal (civil) action.
To seek by request; to make application; to petition; to entreat; to plead.

sue.ety: From Middle English seuen, sewen, siwen, borrowed from Anglo-Norman suer, siwer et al. and Old French sivre (“to follow after”) (modern French suivre), from Vulgar Latin *sequere (“to follow”), from Latin sequi. Cognate with Italian seguire and Spanish seguir. Doublet of segue. Related to suit.

ex.en: The woman goes by the name of Sue.
ex.ja: その女性はスーです。

ex.en: Sue and I have always got on well.
ex.ja: スーと私はいつも仲良くやってきた。

ex.en: Tom and Sue have known each other since 1985.
ex.ja: トムとスーはお互いに１９８５年以来の知り合いだ。

note.ja: 古フランス語 suir（追いかける）から。ラテン語 sequi（続く）と同じ。法廷で追いかける →「訴える」。

en: The condition of being held in a state between two or more forces, which are acting in opposition to each other.
A psychological state of being tense.
To place an object in tension, to pull or place strain on.

ex.ja: 緊張が心臓病の主な原因だ。

ex.en: There are signs of growing tensions between the two countries.
ex.ja: その両国間に緊張が高まりつつある兆しがある。

ex.en: The air was charged with tension.
ex.ja: その場には緊張感がみなぎっていた。

note.ja: tens（伸ばす）+ ion。ぴんと引き伸ばすこと →「緊張・張力」。

en: The act of conducting or carrying out (business, negotiations, plans).
A deal or business agreement.

transaction.ety: Borrowed from Middle French transaction, from Old French transaccion, from Late Latin transactio. By surface analysis, trans- + action.

ex.en: Do you wish to make any other transaction?
ex.ja: 続けてお取り引きなさいますか。

ex.en: He rejoiced at the successful business transaction.
ex.ja: 彼は商売がうまくいったのを喜んだ。

ex.en: There's a lot of money at stake in this transaction.
ex.ja: この取り引きには大金が賭けられている。

en: A twisting force.
Anything twisted, or the act of twisting.
To turn the ends of something, usually thread, rope etc., in opposite directions, often using force.
To join together by twining one part around another.

Related to Saterland Frisian Twist (“discord”), Dutch twist (“twist; strife; discord”), German Low German Twist (“strife; discord”), German Zwist (“turmoil; strife; discord”), Swedish tvist (“quarrel; dispute”), Icelandic tvistur (“deuce”).

ex.en: Why would you say such a twisted thing?
ex.ja: もう、なんでそんなひねくれたこと言うの？

ex.en: This mystery has a plot twist that's completely novel.
ex.ja: このミステリーのトリックは、奇想天外だ。

ex.en: His face was twisted with pain.
ex.ja: 彼の顔は苦痛でいがんだ。

en: Used to express repugnance, disgust, or annoyance.
Used to express inarticulate vocalisations, such as used by a caveman.

ex.en: Ugh, I hate work. I don't wanna go.
ex.ja: 仕事なんか大嫌い。行きたくな〜い。

ex.en: Ugh! I lost my phone again.
ex.ja: げっ！またスマホ落とした。

ex.en: Ugh, what's with you, seriously.
ex.ja: なんだよ、ホントに。

The phenomenon of joblessness in an economy.

ex.ja: 失業率は徐々に上昇するだろう。

en: Oneness: the state or fact of being one undivided entity.
Agreement; harmony.

unity.ety: From Middle English unite, from Anglo-Norman, Old French unité, from Latin ūnitās, from ūnus (“one”) + noun of state suffix -itās, ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *óynos (“one, single”), hence distantly related to one and an. By surface analysis, unite + -y. Displaced native Old English ānnes (literally “oneness”).

ex.en: They live together in unity.
ex.ja: 彼らは仲良く一緒に暮らしている。

ex.en: Unity is our strength!
ex.ja: まとまりは我々の力だ！

ex.en: The figure on the left spoils the unity of the painting.
ex.ja: 左手の人物がその絵の統一性を壊している。

Unhelpful, not useful; pointless (of an action).

ex.ja: あらゆる芸術評論家達は無能であり危険な存在である。

ex.en: All my efforts turned out to be useless.
ex.ja: 努力もすべて、むだであることがわかった。

en: Someone who views a spectacle; an onlooker or spectator.
Someone who watches television.

viewer.ety: From Middle English vewer; equivalent to view + -er.

ex.en: Television viewers see only what the camera shows.
ex.ja: テレビ観戦者はカメラが捕らえるものしか見られない。

ex.en: Television enlightens the viewers as well as entertains them.
ex.ja: テレビは視聴者に娯楽ばかりではなく、知識も与える。

ex.en: The city of Mito was crowded with blossom viewers.
ex.ja: 水戸市は花見客でいっぱいだった。

en: Someone whose job is to speak for someone's case in a court of law; a counsel.
Anyone who argues the case of another; an intercessor.
To plead in favour of; to defend by argument, before a tribunal or the public; to support, vindicate, or recommend publicly.
To encourage support for something.

advocate.ety:
From Middle English advocat, advoket, from Old French advocat, from Latin advocātus (“an advocate”), from the substantivization of the perfect passive participle of advocāre (“to call for”) (see -ate (noun-forming suffix)), from a calque of Ancient Greek παράκλητος (paráklētos) (whence English paraclete).
Doublet of advoke, avocat, avouch, and avow. The verb derives from the noun on the basis of -ate (verb-forming suffix).

ex.en: He advocated to us that the changes be made.
ex.ja: 彼はその改革を実行すべきだと主張した。

ex.en: He advocates reform of university education.
ex.ja: 彼は大学教育の改革を主張している。

ex.en: He advocated the reduction of taxes.
ex.ja: 彼は減税を唱えた。

note.ja: ad（〜へ）+ voc（声・呼ぶ）+ ate。〜のために声を上げる →「主張する・擁護者・弁護士」。

en: That part of a circle which a heavenly body appears to pass through as it moves above and below the horizon.
A continuous part of the circumference of a circle (circular arc) or of another curve.
To move following a curved path.
To shape into an arc; to hold in the form of an arc.

ex.en: The rainbow forms an arc in the sky.
ex.ja: 虹は空に弓じょうにかかる。

en: A reserve or substitute.
A copy of a file or record, stored separately from the original, that can be used to recover the original if it is damaged or destroyed.
Standby, reserve or extra.
That is intended as a backup.

ex.ja: 何かしらの代替案はありますか？

ex.en: No problem. If X happens, we have Y as a backup.
ex.ja: 大丈夫だ。もしXが発生しても、Yでバックアップできる。

en: Having an acrid taste (usually from a basic substance).
Harsh, piercing, acerbic or stinging.
To an intense or severe degree; bitterly.
A liquid or powder, made from bitter herbs, used in mixed drinks or as a tonic.
A type of beer heavily flavored with hops.

ex.en: Bitter medicine will not necessarily do you good.
ex.ja: 必ずしも苦い薬が行く効くとは限らない。

ex.en: Young people must profit from their bitter experiences.
ex.ja: 若者は自分の苦い経験から学ばねばならない。

ex.en: Tom calls his first love a "bitter memory".
ex.ja: トムは、初恋を「ほろ苦い思い出」と言います。

en: Nimble with hands or body; dexterous; skillful; adept.
Quick to understand, learn, and devise or apply ideas; intelligent.

ex.en: He is not as clever as my brother.
ex.ja: 彼は兄ほど賢くない。

ex.en: She is not so much honest as clever.
ex.ja: 彼女は正直と言うより利口だ。

ex.en: I thought he was more clever than honest.
ex.ja: 彼は正直というよりむしろ賢明な人だと私は思った。

en: Without stopping; without a break, cessation, or interruption.
Without intervening space; continued.

continuous.ety: From Latin continuus, from contineō (“hold together”). Displaced native Old English singal.

ex.ja: 延々と続く車の列があった。

ex.en: I have a continuous pain here.
ex.ja: ここに絶え間ない痛みがあります。

ex.en: The Japanese economy recorded more than 60 months of continuous expansion.
ex.ja: 日本経済は連続６０ヶ月以上の拡大を記録した。

To change (something) from one use, function, or purpose to another.
A person who has converted to a religion.
A person who is now in favour of something that they previously opposed or disliked.

ex.ja: その土地は公園に変えられた。
